content.text: Next I'll check the mdx-loader for other places that assume LF line endings.

I fixed the bug in `packages/docusaurus-utils/src/markdownUtils.ts`: two regexes there only matched LF line endings, so files saved with CRLF (the Windows default) broke.

1. **`unwrapMdxCodeBlocks`:** this is the cause of the reported error. The issue's screenshot didn't load for me, but the usual way to write tabs in Markdown is to put the `Tabs` import and `<TabItem>` inside a ```` ```mdx-code-block ```` fence. This function strips that fence before compiling, and its regex required LF line breaks. With CRLF the fence was never removed, so the import never ran and MDX reported `TabItem` as undefined. The regex now accepts `\r?\n` for every line break.
2. **`admonitionTitleToDirectiveLabel`:** a related problem I found while checking. With CRLF, the legacy `:::note Title` syntax captured the trailing `\r` into the title, giving `:::note[Title\r]`. The title now stops before an optional `\r`, using a lookahead so the CRLF line ending itself is kept.

The existing `markdownUtils` tests pass (92/92). I also ran quick checks on CRLF input: an `mdx-code-block` fence unwraps cleanly and `:::note Hi there` becomes `:::note[Hi there]` with its `\r\n` preserved. I didn't add new tests or reproduce the original error with a full site build. I looked through the mdx-loader source for other LF-only assumptions and found none.

`package.json` already had an uncommitted change (a `packageManager` field) before I started; I left it alone.
